# Manifest of the released data and results

Every file under `data/` and `results/` is a file the measurements wrote or read, passed through a reversible renaming: an identifier table (prompt ids of the four hand-written prompt sets, their author values, a few record keys and file names) and a phrase table (free text that named people, roles or the working process). Both are plain string substitutions. A few frozen texts are also *excerpted*: lines or parts of lines that described how the work was organised (who drafted, checked or approved a text, who was told, spending limits, working branches and pauses in the work) are cut, each cut marked in place with "[process note removed]". The hashes recorded inside the files are those of the files before the renaming (README, "Provenance").

## The round trip

Checked when this tree was built, for every file below: no replacement string occurred in the file before the renaming; the inverse renaming of the renamed content gives back the original content byte for byte (for `.gz` files, their decompressed content); and no substitution fell inside a prompt, a sampled reply or a generator output. For an excerpted file the round trip ran on its renamed text, before the cuts, and the build then checked that the cuts are the only difference between that text and the released one. Files checked: 4143. Released as their original bytes (unchanged): 2365. Renamed: 1764. Excerpted: 14, with 73 lines cut in all. All passed.

The tables themselves name the people they remove, so they are not released. The identifier table has 162 entries and the phrase table 790. The replacement side of each entry is listed under "Replacements" below.

## Files

`sha256` is of the released bytes; `private sha256` of the bytes the records hash; `content` columns are of the decompressed content (the same as the bytes for files that are not gzipped). A file of class `unchanged` is byte-identical to its private original; `renamed`, its original under the renaming; `excerpted`, its original under the renaming with the stated number of lines cut. `results/MANIFEST.json` holds the same table for programs.

Where the private path is `same`, the file kept its name. A private path that differs held a word this repository avoids, and is shown unless it held a person's name or a word of the working process.

## Substitutions and cuts in the frozen texts

The texts below were written before the measurements they govern. In them, the group's rounds of work are called stages. Each stage's files sit under folders that keep their original names, `session_003` to `session_010`:

| Prose label | Folders | What that stage did |
|---|---|---|
| stages 1 and 2 | none | pilot work before the first measurements; not released |
| stage 3 | `data/session_003`, `results/session_003` | tested which strings set off the backdoor, and the 102 hand-written prompts |
| stage 4 | `data/session_004`, `results/session_004` | the hand-written red-team search, and the reproduction of Redwood's setting |
| stage 5 | `data/session_005`, `results/session_005` | chose the training setting, and froze the pre-registration |
| stage 6 | `data/session_006`, `results/session_006` | built the red-team data, amended the pre-registration, and ran the standard arm |
| stage 7 | no folders of its own: its texts are under `data/session_006` (`s7_*.md`), its runs under `results/session_006/adv_*` and its seal under `results/session_006/seal` | the first adversarial attempt |
| stage 8 | `data/session_008`, `results/session_008` | the fresh-seed replication |
| stage 9 | `data/session_009`, `results/session_009` | the break-in log-odds of the held-out red-team prompts |
| stage 10 | `data/session_010`, `results/session_010` | the extra-training runs and the every-step scoring |

People are named by role: `[author 1]` to `[author 4]` wrote the hand-written prompt sets whose ids begin `e_hw_`, `m_hw_`, `s0_hw_` and `s1_hw_`, in that order; `[author 5]` wrote and ran the code; `[the lead author]` led the work; `[the senior author]` supervised it. `[an unreleased working note]`, `[an unreleased plan]` and `[an unreleased draft of the amendment]` stand for files of the working process that are not released.

Every Markdown file under `data/` is listed: names, roles and references to unreleased files are replaced, and in the excerpted ones the process wording is cut. For each, its original sha256, its released sha256, and every line that differs from the original, as released (the original lines name people and are not shown; the cut text is not shown).
